title: Layered architecture

overview.why: It keeps code from becoming a tangled mess. If you change your database, you only rewrite the data layer, not the whole app.

why_learning_this: Most real-world companies use this to keep their code organized.
It makes finding and fixing bugs much easier because every job has a specific place.

common_mistakes.title: Skipping layers
common_mistakes.explanation: Making the presentation layer call the database directly. This defeats the purpose and makes the code hard to test.

common_mistakes.title: Mixing logic
common_mistakes.explanation: Putting complex business rules (like calculating discounts) inside the database layer or the presentation layer.

recall_questions.q: Explain layered architecture in your own words, as if to a classmate.
recall_questions.answer: It is a way to organize code into different levels where each level has a specific job, and levels only talk to the one right below them.

recall_questions.q: Can the presentation layer talk directly to the data layer?
recall_questions.answer: No, it must go through the business logic layer first. Layers can only call the layer directly below them.

recall_questions.q: Why is this better than putting all the code in one place?
recall_questions.answer: It keeps the code organized, so if you need to change one part (like the database), you don't have to rewrite everything.

understanding_checks.question: What does this print?
understanding_checks.why: The request goes from the UI, to the logic, to the DB, and then the DB returns 'data' which the logic layer modifies before giving it to the UI.

understanding_checks.question: What architectural rule does this code break?
understanding_checks.answer: The presentation layer (`web_route`) calls the data layer (`db_query`) directly.
understanding_checks.why: In a layered architecture, the top layer must go through the middle business logic layer, not skip it to talk to the DB directly.
